the cytostatic drugs 5-FU, CDDP and ET induce cytotoxicity and genotoxicity in human and zebraﬁsh liver cells in vitro, with the highest sensitivity in zebraﬁ sh cells.
the cytotoxic and genotoxic potential of selected anti-neoplastic agents (5-FU, CDDP, ET) towards human and zebafish cells was investigated.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an alternative in vitro test for genotoxicity testing of cytostatic drugs, which is not currently available.
the potential impact of cytostatic drugs on the aquatic environment and human health.
the identification of the genotoxic potential and mechanism of action of three cytostatic drugs (5-FU, CDDP and ET) in human and zebraﬁsh cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytostatic drugs tested are genotoxic in vitro and that the zebrafish cell line ZFL is a relevant model to assess the genotoxicity of cytostatic drugs.
ZFL and Hep2G cells are equally sensitive to 5-FU-induced genotoxicity and that ZFL cells are more sensitive to ET- and CDDP-induced genotoxicity.
5-FU, ET and CDDP are genotoxic and cytotoxic to human and zebra fish cells, and that the cytotoxicity and genotoxicity of these drugs is dependent on cell line and the type of endpoint used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytostatic drug-induced genotoxicity is a complex process, which depends on the type of the drug, the target cell type, the endpoint and the cell line.
the cytostatic drugs tested in the present study are genotoxic towards zebrafis liver (ZFL), human hepatoma (HEPG2) and human peripheral blood cells (HPBLs), with ZFL cells being the most sensitive.
the cytotoxic and genotoxic effects of the tested drugs were comparable in human and fish cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
zebrafish can be a useful tool to study genotoxic potential of cytostatics and other emerging environmental contaminants.
ZFL cells are sensitive to the genotoxicity of cytostatic drugs, which is in line with the results obtained for mammalian cell lines.
zebrafish can be used as an in vitro model to study the genotoxicity of environmental pollutants.
